title: CRLR/211/2019 of MASTER SHRESHTHA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.211 of 2019
Master Shreshtha, minor aged about 6 years,
Son of Sri Vivek Swaroop .....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and another ...Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. Sachin Panwar, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
 Mr. Lalit Sharma, Advocate for respondent no.2.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 Though this criminal revision seems to be confined from a very
limited prospective, where the revisionist had sought a partial challenge to the
impugned order of 12.04.2019, which has been passed by the Judge, Family
Court Haldwani, District Nainital in Misc. Case No.33 of 2014, Master Shrestha
vs. Vivek Swaroop, whereby while considering the propriety of an application
which was preferred under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. for the grant of maintenance
which was claimed by the revisionist to be paid at the rate of Rs.30,000/-per
month, has been determined to be made payable at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per
month by the impugned order, which is under challenge making a prayer that the
same may be made from the date of application rather from the date of the order.
There had been many other collateral proceedings under different subjects,
which were drawn by the parties to the revision, but that may not be relevant to
be ventured into by this Court at this stage, while deciding this criminal revision,
as the issue of maintenance to a child under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., has got a
different complexity and complexion itself which has to be independently
considered, and particularly under the facts of the present case where the
controversy of the revisionist being a biological son of the respondent no.2, was
a fact which had been established by the judicial order passed by this Court.
Hence, there is no more controversy, that the revisionist is the biological son of
the respondent no.2 herein.

2
2. The revisionist had preferred this revision, while giving a partial
challenge to the impugned order under challenge i.e. dated 12.04.2019, praying
for an enhancement in the grant of maintenance, as it has been determined by
the Judge, Family Court, considering the overall circumstances, including the
aspects pertaining to the respective assets, the respective liabilities, which either
of the parties i.e. the parents of the revisionist have to cater to and the income
which is accruing to the parents of the revisionist. In this long drawn
proceedings of the criminal revision, there had been pleading and counter
pleadings placed on record by the parties and few facts, which now stands
unrebutted and established, on the basis of the pleadings itself are:-
i. That the respondent no.2, who happens to be the biological father of the
revisionist is an income tax payee and has submitted his income tax return
showing his annual income, accruing to him of Rs.12,00,000/- per annum i.e.
equivalent to Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
ii. The counsel for the revisionist has submitted that owing to the various
liabilities, which the guardian of the present revisionist, has to face on account
of her prior matrimonial discord with the earlier husband, she has also to
maintain the other two children born out of the first matrimony.
ii. That during the intervening period, since she i.e. mother/guardian of hte
revisionist has completed law and is now practicing Advocate, in the District
Court of Haldwani, she is not having a very lubricant practice and she has
pleaded in para 6 of the affidavit, filed by the revisionist on 12.04.2022, wherein
it has been asserted, that she is having an income of only approximately
Rs.10,000/- per month and is not an income tax payee and has not been assessed
as such under the Income Tax Act.
3. On the other hand, the counsel for the respondent no.2, had
submitted that no additional financial burden may be harnessed upon respondent
no.2-husband by enhancing the maintenance amount; for the reason being that
he has to maintain his aged parents, coupled with the fact, that another ground of
defence, which the respondent no.2 has taken is that the guardian of the
revisionist i.e. his mother Jyoti, is financially viable and having her own

3
residential accommodation said to have been purchased from her own coffers,
including a four wheel automobile, which was said to have been purchased by
her by making a down payment which itself is a fact, which establishes her
financial liabilities to maintain the revisionist, for which she too is equally
responsible.
4. This Court is of the view, that so far as the responsibility of either
of the parents of the revisionist are concerned, it is equitable in nature, being a
biological father and mother, both own an equal responsibility to maintain a
minor child brought on the earth by them. But maintenance of a minor child has
always to be commensurated with the prevalent market conditions, the inflation
rate and an anticipated investment, which is required to be made for a better and
comfortable upbringing of the child and all these aspects, about the education
and a reasonable upbringing of the child is an equal responsibility of the mother,
as well as the father respondent no.2, herein.
5. The argument of the learned counsel for the respondent no.2, from
the prospective, that the natural mother of the revisionist is having landed, as
such has a car in itself cannot attribute any rationale, which could be availed by
the respondent no.2-husband to deny an appropriate payment of maintenance to
the revisionist, which should be commensurate, to the income accruing to him.
Merely because of the fact that the mother is having an asset, that itself cannot
be a valid reason to deny the maintenance under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. But
looking to the circumstances of the present case which has been brought on
record, this Court is of the view that considering the fact, that since the date of
the institution of the application under Section 125 of C.r.P.C. i.e. on
10.01.2014, the determination of maintenance at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per
month, which has been decided to be paid by the impugned order, which has
been sought to be enhanced, has had to be made payable from the date of the
application itself and not from the date of the judgment, as it has been rendered
by the Family Court on 12.04.2019. This principle has been settled down, that
the determination of maintenance payable to a minor child under Section 125 of
the Cr.P.C. or even for that purposes to the applicant of the application under
Section 125 C.r.P.C. it has had to be determined to be made payable from the

4
date when the application has been filed which in the instant case happens to be
of 10.01.2014.
6. The grievance expressed by the revisionist counsel, is that though
the determination of the maintenance to be paid to the revisionist, at the rate of
Rs.10,000/- which has been directed to be made payable from the date of the
judgment, is apparently bad because, if any maintenance was required to be
determined, it ought to have been made payable with effect from 10.01.2014. I
do not see any reason, not to believe and accept the argument extended by the
learned counsel for the revisionist for paying the maintenance determined by the
Family Court from the date of the application and thus the judgment of
12.04.2019 determining the maintenance to be payable at the rate of Rs.10,000/-
would be reckoned to be made payable from 10.01.2014 i.e. from the date of
filing of the application itself and not from the date of the judgment. Hence, the
arrears at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per month, for the period from 10.01.2014 till
11.04.2019, i.e. date of judgment, would be paid by the respondents as an
arrears as a consequence of today's judgment, within a period of two months
from today.
7. Reverting back to the main issue; where the revisionist has sought
an enhancement in the payment of maintenance under Section 125 of the
Cr.P.C., this Court is of the view, that an isolated interpretation to the respective
income accruing to the guardian, cannot be an exclusive parameter, which could
be determined to be the foundation, to determine the adequacy of maintenance,
which would be payable to a child because maintenance always happens to be a
variable factor depending upon multiple surroundings circumstances, and
reasons including, the proportionate increase in the standard of living and the
price escalation. Since admittedly in the instant case there is no material to the
contrary on record brought by the respondents to deny the fact of his income,
accruing at the rate of Rs.12,00,000/- per annum as per his own income tax
return, which is a fact not rebutted more particularly when the
respondents/father has not been able to rebut the fact of pleading raised by the
mother to the effect that the wife, the guardian of the revisionist is having an
income of only Rs.10,000/- per month.

5
8. This Court is of the view that when the liability, which the
respondent no.2, has to face except for maintaining himself and the aged
parents, he has to equally and appropriately share the burden to maintain the
child and in order to balance the equities after considering the rival contentions
from the various prospective, already discussed above, this Court is of the view
that the determination of maintenance of Rs.10,000/- as determined by the
learned Family Court, in fact there was no plausible rationale, which has been
adopted to determine the same and considering the overall scenario at the
moment, this Court is of the view, that it would meet the ends of justice and will
also balance the equities too between the parties, if the amount of maintenance is
enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.15,000/-, which would be ensured to be paid
by respondent no.2, to the revisionist by 10th of each month. The amount thus
directed to be enhanced by today's order, would obviously be an enhancement,
which would be enforced with effect from 29.04.2019, i.e. from when the
revision was preferred by the revisionist before this Court and the arrears, which
accrues at the rate of Rs.15,000/-, that is the difference of Rs.5,000/- per month
for the period from 29.04.2019 till today i.e. 21.04.2022, would also be ensured
to be paid by the respondent no.2 to the revisionist within a period of two
months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
9. The determination of maintenance to be made payable at the rate of
Rs.15,000/- per month, as directed above would be irrespective of the rights of
the either of the parties to be resorted to seek an appropriate modification or
rectification in the maintenance determined by filing an appropriate proceedings
as permissible under the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure before
the appropriate court.
10. Subject to the aforesaid reasons, the criminal revision stands partly
allowed and the impugned order would stand modified to that extent.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 21.04.2022
